Enrolled Nurse - Operating Theatres

About the role

Are you ready to take your perioperative nursing career to the next level in a growing and evolving environment? Join us at Orange Hospital, the major referral centre for Western NSW, where you'll be part of a high-performing operating theatre team committed to delivering patient-centred care and driving innovation in rural health. It's not often we have vacancies - however nurses who have grown their careers with us have advanced into senior roles in larger hospitals and others are now enjoying a well-earned retirement lifestyle. This is your chance!

With five operating theatres, a procedural room, and a 10-bay recovery unit, our department supports a wide range of surgical specialties including trauma, orthopaedics, upper GI, urology, ENT, obstetrics and gynaecology, and ophthalmology. As a Nurse in our theatres, you'll have the opportunity to rotate across subspecialties, access mentorship, and contribute to research and quality improvement initiatives. 

Whether you're an experienced perioperative nurse looking to shape the future of a growing service, to step into leadership, or are at an early stage in your career - this is your moment. Our team is has a shared vision of clinical excellence, mentorship, and continuity, and we're looking for professionals who want to be part of something meaningful.

You'll need to participate in a 7-day roster, including on-call shifts out of hours, and bring strong communication, attention to detail, and a team-focused mindset. Above all, we want someone who sees the bigger picture - inspiring others, lifting standards, and making rural health stronger.

Come and help us create a thriving, forward-thinking perioperative team - and build a career you'll be proud of.

Randstad is proud to partner with Queensland Rail (QR) on a major recruitment drive to source engineering professionals. As part of this major recruitment drive, we are looking to identify an experienced Principal Telecommunications Network Engineer - ETCS for the ETCS Sequence Alliance (Embedded) division.  
  QR has a current project pipeline of over A$15 billion, and this is expected to grow exponentially in the build-up to the 2032 Brisbane Olympic and Paralympic Games.. As a result of this significant investment, the need to secure in-house technical and engineering resources is paramount to support their critical technology rollouts. This includes ensuring that European Train Control Systems (ETCS) telecommunications networks are technically robust and compliant across the network.  
  What You'll Do  
  The Principal Telecommunications Network Engineer - ETCS will provide specialist engineering services and technical leadership to project-based teams. You will be responsible for ensuring that ETCS telecommunications networks are technically robust, commercially optimized, and seamlessly integrated.  
 
  Drive Engineering Excellence  : Monitor and influence ETCS Cross River Rail (CRR) telecommunications data system projects, ensuring peak performance levels are achieved at competitive costs. You will ensure that integration into the QR data network never compromises reliability, availability, or maintainability.  
  Coach & Inspire:   Lead the facilitation of technical training and competency development for telecommunications office and field staff, ensuring a powerful capability uplift and compliance across teams.  
  Innovate & Optimize  : Ensure technical standards and procedures are meticulously documented and applied in accordance with Queensland Rail Quality Assurance and Improvement Principles.  
  Thought Leader  : Provide strategic technical leadership and advice to business groups, technical staff, and external stakeholders, ensuring complex network solutions align perfectly with QR's operational requirements.  
   Uphold Integrity : Champion strict compliance with professional engineering practices, Queensland Rail standards, and all corporate legal and safety obligations.  
 
  What We Are Looking For  
  We are looking for a strong implementor in the network engineering space who brings a deep understanding of data communications, commercial acumen, and high-level stakeholder management skills.  
 
  Qualifications  : A Bachelor of Engineering (Electrical & Electronic)   AND   ideally   current Registered Professional Engineer Queensland (RPEQ) status   or   have the necessary qualifications and experience to attain it. IE: have CEng or Professional Engineer status with Engineers Australia.  
  Network Telecoms Experience:   Extensive knowledge of LAN/WAN data communications, and physical network security applicable to a railway network. You must bring high-level skills in the design, system configuration, construction, auditing, commissioning, integration, and technical support of telecommunications network systems. Candidates would ideally come from a client or contractor background and have strong implementation experience.  
  Analytical & Technical Depth:   Extensive knowledge of telecommunications performance and integration principles, combined with strong analytical and problem-solving skills to keep ETCS CRR projects operationally effective.  
  Commercial Acumen:   A proven track record of delivering business-focused technical and professional network solutions that bring tangible commercial value to the business.  
  Soft Skills & Influence  : High levels of interpersonal, influencing, and negotiation skills.  
 
  Queensland Rail is a progressive organisation that promotes a flexible working environment to allow for a healthy work-life balance. It actively prioritizes the development of its people in a supportive, diverse, and inclusive work culture.

  Competitive remuneration packages

Bourke Multi Purpose Service

 

About the role
If you are a caring and skilled midwife who thrives on variety and likes to be out and about, we've got a great opportunity for you. 

As a community midwife in the heart of the thriving rural town of Bourke you'll be building relationships, providing information and giving support to the women of the Bourke district and their babies. 

As well as being actively involved in giving antenatal advice and helping parent prepare for birth, you will attend to postnatal needs for the first 10 days post-birth, mostly in the homes of the new mothers. You will help new mothers look after themselves and their baby including parenting, infant feeding, settling, sleep and other related topics as guided by the needs, expectations and aspirations of the women in your care. 

In a small, close knit team you will be well supported and your dedication will be seen and appreciated. You will be an integral member of the community and you'll see not only the results of your care, but the appreciation of the community of the role you play in their health. 

This truly is a role where you will broaden your scope, develop new skills and supercharge your career. 

About Bourke 

Bourke is a beautiful historic town set on the banks of the Darling River -one of Australia's most important rivers. The Bourke Shire (local government area) has an area of approximately 43,000 square kilometres and is home to around 3000 people, with the Shire's prosperity built around the pastoral, irrigation, tourism and service industries which are strongly supported by a wide range of attractions and activities. 

The community of Bourke is welcoming and warm, and our hospital staff are considered to be very special. Bourke locals spend their leisure time in sporting pursuits (soccer, rugby, netball, cricket, swimming and golf are available) camping in the remote bush, bushwalking, canoeing, birdwatching and fishing. There is always something to do and people to make new friends. 

The Bourke shire is rich in Indigenous cultural history. Traditionally country of the Ngemba-Ngempa people, Bourke is now home to around 24 different recognised Indigenous language groups. Many of Bourke's Indigenous peoples are Wangkumara people from the Tibooburra region, but also include those from the Murawarri, Barkindji- Gurnuand Yandruwandha Nations to name a few. 

Visit our Bourke Community page to hear from community members who live and work in Bourke. 

Helping you move to Western NSW 

The Welcome Experience is a free NSW Government service supporting essential workers (and their families) who are considering applying for or have accepted a job in regional NSW. 

Local Connectors can help you with everything from the practicalities of moving, finding housing, education, social and cultural connections, leisure and recreation, employment for partners and healthcare.

About the Role 



We are seeking an experienced and passionate healthcare worker to join us as the Family Violence Program Officer within our Patient Experience Office at Monash Health. 




This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to organisational and system-wide change, strengthening Monash Health's response to family violence, child safeguarding and elder abuse. Working in partnership with the Family Violence Lead and clinical services across the organisation, you will play a key role in building workforce capability, embedding evidence-informed practice and supporting implementation of Victoria's family violence reforms. 




The role supports implementation of Victorian family violence reforms, promotes practice excellence and drives continuous improvement across the health service. Based primarily at Monash Medical Centre Clayton, this position offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact at both a service and system level.

The Patient Experience Office (PEO) at Monash Health champions the voices of patients, families, carers and communities to ensure care is person-centered, compassionate and responsive to individual needs. Through consumer partnerships, co-design initiatives, feedback programs and patient information resources, the team helps shape and improve healthcare services across the organisation. The PEO works closely with consumers and staff to translate lived experiences into meaningful improvements in care delivery, communication and health outcomes. 




The Family Violence Program leads Monash Health's organisational response to family violence, child safeguarding and elder abuse. As the Family Violence Program Officer, you'll have the opportunity to shape how one of Australia's largest public health services responds to family violence. Working alongside a dedicated and highly respected team within the Patient Experience Office, you'll influence practice across the organisation, helping to create safer outcomes for patients, families and staff. Joining Monash Health means you'll:

This position offers 12 months experience in Rural Generalist Medicine in a busy procedural facilitiy. This post would suit Rural Generalist Trainees looking for experience in a busy regional trauma centre and for trainees wishing to gain experience in the management of acute general medical, emergency medicine and critically unwell patients. Trainees will be given responsibilities and opportunities for autonomous practice commensurate with their experience.

Mudgee Health Service provides inpatient and community-based services as part of Western NSW Local Health District. The Facility has an emergency department with a doctor available to attend onsite. Virtual care is available 24-7 through the use of our vCare camera system ensuring all unwell patients can receive emergency care after hours.

The hospital has a general ward that caters for Medical and Surgical patients with a capacity as well as a Maternity Unit providing care for well women, higher risk pregnancies are referred to Dubbo Health Service or other appropriate facilities according to patient needs. There are two Operating theatres. Theatres operate an average of three days per week with on call services provided 24-7 for emergency obstetrics.

Mudgee Health Service provides Acute and Sub-Acute Inpatient services which include:

Medical, Surgical, Rehabilitation, Maternity, Palliative Care, Renal Dialysis, Chemotherapy, Medical Imaging and Ambulatory care.

The township of Mudgee has a population of approximately 11,000 residents and is 183 kilometres northeast of Orange and 126 kilometres southeast of Dubbo.

Mudgee is a popular tourist town known for its food, wine, picturesque countryside, and historic buildings. The region also has several coal mines approximately 30 minutes from town that provide a large number of jobs to the local community.

Mudgee is part of the Mid-Western Regional Local Government Area, which also includes Gulgong and Rylstone. The projected population for Mudgee and surrounds is expected to increase by 8.4% from 2023 to 2033.
